# sftp-loadtest

> Multi-protocol load testing for SFTP, FTP, and FTPS. Single-binary CLI/server plus a native desktop app, sharing one engine. Real files, multi-worker SSH fan-out, optional SHA-256 round-trip byte verification, streaming CSV + JSON reports.

sftp-loadtest exercises file-transfer servers under realistic operator workloads. It uploads files (synthetic random bytes or real source files from disk) at a configured files-per-minute rate, optionally polls for the server's processing-suffix rename (`foo.txt` → `foo.txt#<trackid>`), then optionally pulls the processed file back through a download phase and matches it to the upload by track-id or by filename pattern. Per-file CSV plus per-run JSON metadata stream to disk as the run progresses, so memory stays flat over 24-hour tests.

Use it when your workload is SFTP / FTP / FTPS file transfer with a server-side processing step — typical of Managed File Transfer (MFT) platforms, EDI gateways, partner-onboarding pipelines, and any setup where the server renames-then-moves processed files.

Do **not** use it for HTTP, gRPC, WebSocket, or database load — k6, Locust, vegeta, JMeter cover those domains and this tool does not.

## HTTP API (CLI/server SKU)

| Endpoint | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `GET /healthz` | liveness — `{status, uptime_sec, active_run, active_run_id}` |
| `GET /api/host` | one-shot host capacity (CPU, RAM, FD limit, NICs) |
| `GET /api/status` | live run state, metrics, error counts, disabled users, FD-in-use |
| `GET /api/runs` | history — both live (in-memory) and historical (on-disk) runs |
| `POST /api/start` | start a run with a JSON config |
| `POST /api/stop` | stop the active run |
| `GET /api/report.csv?run=<id>` | streaming CSV download (live or historical) |
| `POST /api/probe` | TCP / SSH / SFTP / folder-list pre-flight check |
| `POST /api/schedule` | queue a future run |
| `GET /api/schedules` | list pending schedules |
| `POST /api/schedule/cancel?id=<id>` | cancel a pending schedule |
| `POST /api/cluster/start` | fan-out a single config across N worker URLs |

Default bind: `127.0.0.1:8080`. SSH-tunnel for remote access (`ssh -L 8080:localhost:8080 user@host`). No web-UI authentication shipped; front with nginx / Caddy basic-auth for multi-tenant.

## Authentication to the target server

- **SFTP**: password (per-user CSV row) or SSH public-key (one PEM applied to all users in the run; per-user keys are a v2 follow-up). Host-key TOFU is **on by default** — first connection captures the SHA-256 fingerprint, subsequent connections refuse on mismatch.
- **FTP**: password only (protocol is plaintext; prefer FTPS for non-lab use).
- **FTPS**: password + leaf-certificate fingerprint capture. UI consent prompt for first-trust is a v2 follow-up; the "Trust self-signed cert" toggle covers lab use today.

## Server contract for round-trip mode

For the round-trip story to work, the target server must:

1. Append `#<trackid>` to each processed file's name (anywhere in the upload folder).
2. Place the processed file in the configured download folder (e.g. `outbox`).

Without this, uploads will succeed but the download phase sees nothing — the tool will not invent files.

## Reports

- **CSV** (one row per uploaded file): track-id, user, filename, upload-start/end, upload-bytes, processing-time-min, download-start/end, download-bytes, latency-ms, error-code, optional SHA-256 hash (upload and download legs).
- **JSON** (one object per run): `total_files`, `total_bytes`, `overall_mbps`, `peak_window_mbps`, `failed_files`, `dispatch_skips`, `latency.upload.{p50,p95,p99,p99_9}_ns`, `stop_reason` (`duration` / `user` / `speed-floor` / `max-failures`), `concurrent_runs_at_peak`, `host_capacity` (CPU, RAM, FD limit), `suggestions` (narrative).

## Alerting

Slack, generic webhook, and SMTP alerts on configurable triggers: failure count, p99 ms, error rate %, dispatch skips, hash mismatch, speed-floor stop. Configured per run; alerts fire from the runner, not from a separate agent.

## Limitations

- Single concurrent run per process — run multiple processes on different ports, or use Cluster fan-out for true parallelism.
- Per-user SSH keys: one PEM is shared across all users (v2 follow-up).
- No SSH-agent integration — paste a PEM, no socket-based forwarding.
- FTPS cert TOFU: fingerprint capture today, UI consent prompt is v2.
- S3, WebDAV, HTTP transports: not supported (use the right tool).

## Performance posture (v0.19.0)

- Pipelined SFTP writes (`pkg/sftp` opened with `UseConcurrentWrites(true)`) — estimated 2–5× per-file throughput on long-haul links where round-trip time was the binding constraint pre-v0.19; localhost mocks won't show much because RTT is sub-microsecond.
- CSV stream writer batches flushes (`WriteRowsBatch` cuts flush syscalls 50–150× during high-fpm windows).
- `LocalDisk` sink wraps the file with a 1 MiB `bufio.Writer` (1.1 M syscalls → ~36 k over a 36 GB/hour persistence run).

## Form factors

- **webui SKU**: single CLI binary, hosts the web UI on a TCP port. For lab racks, CI, long-running scheduled tests, server installs.
- **desktop-app SKU** (Wails-based): native macOS / Linux / Windows window, no allocated port. For client laptops, ad-hoc tests, shipping to non-technical users.

Both share the same load engine, UI, security model, and CSV report format. Released in lockstep — every tagged release contains both.

## Releases

Pre-built binaries for macOS (Apple Silicon, Intel), Linux (amd64, arm64), Windows (amd64). Each download is a single binary or single `.app` bundle; URLs follow the `releases/latest/download/<asset>` pattern so README links self-update.
